title: Faculty narrative feedback in the vascular surgery entrustable professional activity pilot is disproportionately focused on patient care and medical knowledge competencies.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Performance feedback is critical to guide vascular surgery trainees' skill development across competency domains. Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity. It is unclear how faculty use this information to guide and focus the content of their feedback. We sought to identify the core competencies reflected in narrative feedback in a multi-institutional study of EPA assessments. METHODS: EPA assessments were collected during a 3-month national Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. Trainees were rated on their performance of EPAs on a 4-point Likert scale and faculty had the opportunity to provide feedback. Narrative feedback was qualitatively analyzed using focused coding guided by the Vascular Surgery Milestones 2.0 framework. Feedback was coded using the six ACGME core competencies-patient care (PC), medical knowledge (MK), professionalism, interpersonal and communication skills, practice-based learning and improvement, and systems-based practice (SBP)-to characterize the domains emphasized in feedback. Quality assessment scores were assigned to all narrative feedback using the Quality of Assessment of Learning framework. Descriptive analysis was completed using R (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). RESULTS: Faculty completed 983 EPA assessments of 78 trainees across 17 institutions (n = 16 integrated residencies, n = 12 fellowships). Narrative feedback was included in 760 (77%) assessments. Feedback most frequently addressed PC (n = 662, 82%), followed by MK (n = 418, 55%), whereas feedback about practice-based learning and improvement (n = 42, 6%), interpersonal and communication skills (n = 42,6%), professionalism (n = 20, 3%), and SBP (n = 26, 3%) were less common. Most assessments were completed for postgraduate year-3 (29%) and postgraduate year-4 trainees (22%). Most assessments occurred during the intraoperative phase of care (88%), with relatively few occurring in preoperative (7%) or postoperative (5%) phases. In addition, feedback-referencing PC was associated with higher odds of high-quality feedback in comparison with feedback about the other competencies (odds ratio, 25.56; 95% confidence interval, 6.13-106.55). CONCLUSIONS: In this multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, faculty most frequently provided trainees with feedback on their performance of PC and MK competencies. Feedback on performance related to SBP was infrequently provided and, when provided, was of generally low quality. This has important implications for the use of EPAs to inform ACGME Milestones ratings and suggests alternative assessment tools will continue to be needed to capture performance across all competency domains required of a physician.

Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed.

title: Beyond Absolute Blood Pressure Targets During Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Narrative Review of Intraprocedural Hemodynamics.
abstract: Hemodynamic management is a central component of procedural care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) during endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT. However, definitions, baseline reference pressures, measurement intervals, and BPV metrics vary widely across studies, and associations with neurological outcomes are inconsistent. Importantly, these systemic BP parameters do not directly establish cerebral perfusion. This limitation supports investigating cerebral autoregulation as a complementary, patient-specific assessment. Evidence linking individualized autoregulatory limits to outcomes remains predominantly post-EVT, with very limited evidence during the pre-recanalization phase under anesthesia. This review examines intraprocedural BP during EVT under anesthesia beyond absolute pressure targets. It considers relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, pressure-time burden, BPV, and individualized autoregulatory limits in relation to cerebral perfusion. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed for studies evaluating hemodynamics during EVT under anesthesia, supplemented by screening of selected reference lists. Studies examining intraprocedural BP targets, relative changes, hypotension duration, pressure-time burden, and BPV in relation to neurological or imaging outcomes under anesthesia were prioritized, with emphasis on the pre-recanalization period. Post-EVT hemodynamic studies were not included in the primary synthesis, except where they informed the discussion of cerebral autoregulation and future research. Intraprocedural hemodynamic variables during EVT characterize different aspects of systemic arterial-pressure exposure that may be relevant to cerebral perfusion in the ischemic penumbra. Absolute pressure, relative change, magnitude and duration of hypotension, pressure-time burden, and BPV should be regarded as complementary rather than interchangeable measures. Differences in reference pressures, definitions, measurement intervals, exposure periods relative to recanalization, and anesthesia techniques limit comparisons and standardization across studies. Future prospective studies, particularly during general anesthesia (GA), should integrate clearly defined systemic BP metrics with dynamic cerebral autoregulation. This may help determine which parameters or combinations best reflect cerebral physiological vulnerability. Individualized autoregulation-guided BP targets remain investigational and require prospective validation before they can inform routine clinical hemodynamic management.

Current guideline recommendations predominantly provide absolute blood pressure (BP) targets for intraprocedural management. Studies have also examined relative BP reduction, the magnitude and duration of hypotensive exposure, and blood pressure variability (BPV), providing additional measures of systemic hemodynamic exposure during EVT.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR. METHODS: Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared. RESULTS: A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV patients demonstrated greater improvements in left ventricular function and transvalvular hemodynamics, suggesting that bicuspid morphology itself does not confer an adverse long-term prognostic effect in appropriately selected patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR. TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02803294.

title: One-year outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis in acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed up for up to 1 year or until death. RESULTS: A total of 724 patients were included in this study: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of patients. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index of >0 (73% vs 60%; P < .001). Age and the rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between the groups. The median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, interquartile range, 46-89) than for CDT (58 minutes, interquartile range, 40-77; P = .003). The median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs 0%; P = .048), and CDT was associated with higher intensive care unit admission rates (83% vs 36%; P < .001). However, the 30-day mortality rate was similar between the groups (CDT: 2.6% vs MT: 4.6%; P = .27). Additionally, the 1-year incidence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (MT: 4.5% vs CDT: 3.4%; P = .69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%; P = .31), and all-cause mortality (MT: 7.8% vs CDT: 5.8%; P = .41) were not statistically significantly different between the MT and CDT groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable 30-day mortality rates and 1-year recurrence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and PE. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative cardiac complications, and CDT was associated with more frequent intensive care unit admission.

However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

title: Contemporary Outcomes of Isolated Common Femoral Endarterectomy in the Endovascular Era.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Common femoral endarterectomy (CFE) remains the reference treatment for common femoral artery (CFA) occlusive disease, yet contemporary real-world data focused specifically on isolated CFE remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile, operative characteristics, and outcomes of isolated CFE performed in a tertiary vascular surgery center, with particular emphasis on postoperative complications, reintervention and occlusion, as well as the possible influence of wound closure technique and hemostatic adjunct use on local morbidity. METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted including consecutive patients who underwent isolated CFE between January 2013 and December 2023. Baseline characteristics, clinical presentation, lesion complexity, operative details, postoperative complications, reinterventions, and postoperative occlusion were analyzed. Lesions were classified according to Trans-Atlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II). Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to assess freedom from occlusion, while Cox regression was performed to explore factors associated with postoperative occlusion. Fisher's exact test was used to assess associations between wound closure technique, hemostatic adjunct use, and postoperative complications. RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent 100 isolated CFEs. The mean age was 68.5 ± 9 years, 89% were male, and 63% presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Most lesions were classified as TASC A-B (68%). The median follow up was 3.5 years (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.2-3.9). Early postoperative complications were predominantly local, including groin hematoma (4%), lymphatic leakage (4%), lymphocele (5%), pseudoaneurysm (2%), and infection (8%). Overall, 18% of procedures required reintervention, with 14% undergoing open and 4% endovascular reintervention. Nine occlusive events occurred during follow up. Estimated freedom from occlusion was 100% at 30 days, 96% at 1 year, and 86% at 5 years. TASC C-D lesions showed a numerically higher occlusion rate than TASC A-B lesions (12.5% vs. 7.4%; OR, 1.80), although this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.462). In univariable Cox regression, aspirin therapy was the only variable significantly associated with lower risk of postoperative occlusion (hazard ratio [HR], 0.20; P = 0.026). Neither intradermal wound closure nor hemostatic adjunct use was significantly associated with postoperative complications. CONCLUSION: Isolated CFE remains a safe and durable treatment for CFA occlusive disease, with low rates of early local complications, acceptable reintervention rates and good freedom from occlusion during follow up. These findings support the continued role of isolated CFE as the reference treatment for CFA disease in the endovascular era.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Common femoral endarterectomy (CFE) remains the reference treatment for common femoral artery (CFA) occlusive disease, yet contemporary real-world data focused specifically on isolated CFE remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile, operative characteristics, and outcomes of isolated CFE performed in a tertiary vascular surgery center, with particular emphasis on postoperative complications, reintervention and occlusion, as well as the possible influence of wound closure technique and hemostatic adjunct use on local morbidity. METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted including consecutive patients who underwent isolated CFE between January 2013 and December 2023.

title: Use of smart glasses for ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization in adults: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Head-mounted displays can be integrated with ultrasonography to overlay the image in the operator's field of view, improving hand-eye coordination during invasive procedures. The clinical efficacy of smart glasses for central venous catheterization (CVC) remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether using smart glasses can improve efficiency compared to conventional ultrasound-guided CVC. METHODS: This prospective, single-blinded, controlled study enrolled adult patients who underwent elective surgery requiring CVC. Patients were assigned to either the ultrasound screen (control) or smart glasses group using stratified randomization according to operator qualification. The primary outcome was the overall CVC procedural time. Secondary outcomes included ultrasound scanning and venous access time, number of needle redirections and probe repositionings, procedural success and complication rates. RESULTS: In total, 124 patients were analyzed. The overall procedural time was significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to that in the control group (158 [140, 189] s vs. 134 [117,150] s; median difference, 26.0 s; 95% CI, [16.0-37.0] s, P < 0.001). Specifically, the ultrasound scanning time (median difference, 3.0 s, P = 0.004), venous access time (median difference, 2.0 s, P = 0.013), number of needle redirections (median difference, 1.0, P = 0.003) and probe repositionings (median difference, 0.0, P = 0.005) were significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to those in the control group. However, the success and complication rates were comparable between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Smart glasses modestly improved procedural efficiency in ultrasound-guided CVC, potientially for novices, without improving success or complication rates. Larger-sample studies with more diverse operators and patients are warranted. title: Endovascular Management With a Fenestration Technique of an Iatrogenic Thoracic Chronic Type B Aortic Dissection.
abstract: We report the case of an 86-year-old woman who developed an intraoperative type B aortic dissection during ascending aortic replacement for an ascending aortic aneurysm. Postoperative imaging demonstrated an uncomplicated dissection extending to the infrarenal aorta. At 10 weeks, follow-up imaging revealed rapid aneurysmal expansion of the false lumen. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed with adjunctive cerebrospinal fluid drainage, rapid pacing, and image fusion guidance. An intimal fenestration technique was used to optimize the distal sealing zone, extending the disruption from a pre-existing re-entry tear. A type Ib endoleak necessitated additional stent-graft deployment, which in turn caused occlusion of the left renal and superior mesenteric arteries. The STABILISE technique (stent-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination in aortic dissection repair) with a PETTICOAT (Provisional Extension To Induce Complete Attachment) bare stent restored renal perfusion, and targeted stenting re-established mesenteric flow. A postprocedural pseudoaneurysm was managed conservatively and resolved with spontaneous thrombosis within 48 hours. The patient was discharged on postoperative day seven, asymptomatic, with complete exclusion of the dissection, patent visceral vessels, and no endoleak confirmed at six-week follow-up. This case illustrates that combining distal flap fenestration with STABILISE relamination and a comprehensive endovascular toolkit can successfully manage complex chronic type B aortic dissections, even in elderly, high-risk patients-provided that adequate perioperative safety measures and a broad endovascular armamentarium are available to address unanticipated complications.

Postoperative imaging demonstrated an uncomplicated dissection extending to the infrarenal aorta. At 10 weeks, follow-up imaging revealed rapid aneurysmal expansion of the false lumen.

title: Detection of serum amyloid A in Saliva of patients with internal carotid artery stenosis: a pilot study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine whether serum amyloid A (SAA) is detectable in saliva of patients with internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis and to investigate the relationship between salivary and serum SAA levels across the perioperative period of carotid endarterectomy (CEA). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Six patients with asymptomatic ICA stenosis (60-99%) undergoing CEA were enrolled. Periodontal status was assessed at enrolment and used to characterise the cohort and document potential oral inflammatory confounding of salivary SAA. Salivary and serum SAA, C-reactive protein (CRP), and lipid parameters were measured before CEA, on postoperative day 2, and 30-45 days postoperatively using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and standard laboratory methods. RESULTS: SAA was detectable in all saliva samples. Serum SAA increased after surgery and did not decline at follow-up, whereas salivary SAA showed a progressive decline (repeated measures ANOVA: F(2,4) = 25.01, p = 0.005). A strong negative correlation was observed between changes in serum and salivary SAA (Pearson's r = - 0.976, p = 0.004). CONCLUSIONS: In this small pilot cohort, SAA was detectable in all saliva samples, and salivary concentrations decreased across the perioperative time points while serum SAA did not show a parallel decline. The observed inverse serum-saliva association should be interpreted cautiously given the very small sample size, absence of a control group, and potential oral and sampling confounders. These findings support the feasibility of measuring salivary SAA in this clinical setting and warrant confirmation in larger controlled studies.

title: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Hospitalized Medical Patients: A Narrative Review of Risk Stratification, Treatment Duration, and Bleeding Trade-Offs.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients, yet decisions about who should receive prophylaxis - and for how long - remain far from settled. This review synthesizes evidence from 22 sources, including randomized trials, prospective and retrospective cohorts, systematic reviews, and major society guidelines, addressing risk stratification, in-hospital anticoagulant prophylaxis, extended-duration direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), the associated bleeding trade-offs, and real-world implementation. The evidence broadly supports pharmacologic prophylaxis during hospitalization for appropriately selected, acutely ill medical patients with acceptable bleeding risk, with the strongest randomized evidence favoring low-molecular-weight heparin during the inpatient period. That benefit comes with trade-offs worth weighing carefully, since even well-supported regimens carry a measurable increase in bleeding risk alongside their protective effect. Commonly used risk-assessment tools have real limitations as well: the Padua and IMPROVE scores offer a useful clinical framework, but head-to-head comparison shows both discriminate poorly between patients who will and won't develop VTE, and real-world implementation data reveal frequent misclassification and inconsistent dose administration. Extended-duration anticoagulation after discharge follows a similar pattern across the major DOAC trials in this space - fewer thrombotic events, but more bleeding, without a clear survival benefit. Taken together, this evidence points toward a risk-adapted rather than protocol-driven approach: assess VTE and bleeding risk at admission, initiate appropriate inpatient prophylaxis, reassess as the clinical picture changes, confirm that prescribed doses are actually being given, and reserve extended anticoagulation after discharge for carefully selected patients rather than applying it as a default. Meaningful progress in this area will likely come less from another static risk score and more from models that can track mobility, bleeding risk, and treatment response dynamically over the course of a hospital stay.

title: Interventional Management of Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Portal Vein Tumor Thrombosis: Are There Differences Between East and West?
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes current evidence on interventional therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT), compares the treatment strategies between East and West, and proposes a practical framework for patient selection in the immunotherapy era of HCC. RECENT FINDINGS: Although systemic therapy remains the primary treatment for advanced HCC with PVTT, selected interventional therapies may provide additional value in carefully chosen patients with preserved liver function, liver-dominant disease, anatomically targetable PVTT, and adequate or reconstructable portal venous flow. Interventional options include transarterial chemoembolization, hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy, transarterial radioembolization/selective internal radiation therapy, radiotherapy, portal vein stenting, and iodine-125 seed-based endovascular brachytherapy. Eastern and Western practice patterns differ mainly in the threshold for locoregional intensification, technical platform availability, and interpretation of the available evidence. Eastern and Western approaches increasingly share the principle that systemic therapy is the treatment backbone for advanced HCC with PVTT. The key clinical question is how interventional therapy should be integrated for selected patients rather than whether it should replace systemic therapy. Optimal management should be individualized through multidisciplinary decision-making based on PVTT extent, portal venous flow, liver function, intrahepatic and extrahepatic tumor burden, treatment goals, and institutional expertise. Future studies should standardize reporting of PVTT classification, portal vein patency, collateral circulation, liver reserve, tumor distribution, systemic therapy context, and treatment sequencing.

title: Selective endovascular aortic repair in connective tissue disease patients within a multidisciplinary program achieves comparable outcomes in high-risk patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Endovascular aortic repair (ENDO) in patients with connective tissue disease (CTD) has historically been discouraged in society guidelines because of durability concerns. However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. METHODS: In this study, 92 patients with CTD undergoing aortic intervention at a single high-volume aortic center between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Patients were stratified by ENDO (n = 50) vs open repair (OPEN; n = 42). The primary outcome was freedom from aortic-related mortality (ARM). The secondary outcomes included technical success, complications, secondary aortic intervention (SAI), and overall survival. A prespecified contemporary analysis (2018-2023) was conducted to evaluate the outcomes following the establishment of a multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate survival and freedom from SAI. RESULTS: The mean age was 48 ± 16 years, and 34% (n = 31) were female. Diagnoses included Marfan syndrome (69%), Loeys-Dietz syndrome (15%), familial aortopathy (11%), and vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (5%). Patients who underwent ENDO more frequently had prior sternotomy/open cardiac surgery (68% vs 19%; P < .0001), prior aortic surgery (70% vs 33%; P = .0007), and urgent presentation (50% vs 14%; P = .0004). Overall, 60% of these patients were deemed unfit for open repair by the multidisciplinary aortic team because of physiologic risk, anatomic complexity, or urgent presentation. The technical success rate was lower after ENDO (82% vs 98%; P = .02), and the 30-day reintervention rate was higher (16% vs 0%; P = .01). The median follow-up period was 2.3 years [interquartile range, 1.1-4.7]. SAIs occurred more frequently following ENDO (56% vs 12%; P = .0001), including planned staged procedures (ENDO: 28.6% vs OPEN: 20%; P = 1) and unplanned reinterventions (ENDO: 71.4% vs OPEN: 80%; P = 1). In the full cohort, patients undergoing ENDO had lower 3-year survival rates (71% ± 7% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .03). In the contemporary cohort, survival at 2 years following ENDO (n = 17) was poorer than that after OPEN (n = 42), although the difference did not reach significance (71% ± 14% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .1). Similarly, the rate of freedom from ARM was lower, but not significantly different (88% ± 12% vs 98% ± 2%; log-rank P = .4). CONCLUSIONS: Open repair remains the gold standard for connective tissue disease-associated aortic disease. In carefully selected high-risk patients, ENDO serves as a complementary strategy with acceptable contemporary survival and comparable freedom from ARM. Higher secondary intervention rates reflect both planned staged repair and unplanned surveillance-detected failure modes, underscoring the need for lifelong follow-up within multidisciplinary programs.

However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program.

title: Impact of Undertreated Antithrombotic Therapy on Adverse Patient Outcomes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
abstract: Antithrombotic therapy undertreatment includes omission, nonadherence, underdosing, and clinical circumstances that result in subtherapeutic antithrombotic levels. Antithrombotic undertreatment has profound implications for patient safety, public health, and healthcare costs. Due to deviation from evidence-based clinical practice, misperceptions of bleeding versus thrombotic risk, and inequities in healthcare access, many patients with atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, or peripheral artery disease remain untreated or receive suboptimal anticoagulant dosing. Antithrombotic undertreatment has been shown to increase rates of ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, recurrent thrombosis, and mortality. Real-world data continue to highlight substantial gaps in care, which appear to be magnified in patients with inequity in social determinants of health. The emergence of antithrombotic stewardship, in concert with growing bodies of literature on antithrombotic agent underdosing, represents a transformative opportunity to address these gaps through structured, interprofessional, and evidence-based approaches. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, healthcare professionals are well positioned to enhance patient health and safety by recognizing and recommitting to reducing antithrombotic undertreatment.

title: Artificial intelligence for the detection of large vessel occlusion stroke and workflow optimization: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) tools on workflow efficiency, treatment times, and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke. METHODS: We included observational studies that assessed the implementation of AI-based tools in the management of patients with suspected or confirmed LVO stroke. Eligible studies reported workflow, treatment, safety, or functional outcomes. Data were extracted on thrombolysis rates, CTA-to-arterial puncture time, door-to-puncture time, endovascular treatment (EVT) access, reperfusion success, symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), mortality, and functional independence (mRS 0-2) at 90 days. Random-effects models were applied to calculate pooled mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. AI implementation significantly reduced workflow delays: CTA-to-puncture time decreased by -40.20 minutes (95% CI -66.41 to -13.99; P<0.01) and door-to-puncture time by -23.17 minutes (95% CI -38.71 to -7.63; P<0.01). Thrombolysis administration showed no difference (RR 0.79; 95% CI 0.57-1.09; P=0.15). Similarly, no significant effects were observed for EVT access (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.66-1.44; P=0.89), reperfusion success (RR 1.06; 95% CI 1.00-1.12; P=0.06), sICH (RR 0.63; 95% CI 0.30-1.35; P=0.23), or mortality (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.38-1.37; P=0.32). However, AI-based workflows significantly improved functional independence at 90 days (RR 1.55; 95% CI 1.12-2.15; P=0.008). CONCLUSIONS: AI tools significantly improve treatment times and functional independence in acute LVO stroke without increasing adverse events.

METHODS: We included observational studies that assessed the implementation of AI-based tools in the management of patients with suspected or confirmed LVO stroke. Eligible studies reported workflow, treatment, safety, or functional outcomes.

title: A single-cell census of pulmonary endarterectomies tissue across different anatomical regions in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remains one of potentially curative options for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). The operation can remove proximal thromboembolic materials and their secondary branches. However, the cellular landscape and pathological features across different anatomical regions remain limited understood. METHODS: Ten patients with CTEPH undergoing PEA surgery and six reference distal pulmonary arteries were conducted single-cell transcriptomics to profile the cellular composition of the main and its bifurcate portion. RESULTS: Pronounced muscularised and fibrotic thrombi organisation were presented in the main portion, and the proportion of mononuclear phagocytes was significantly increased. Inflammatory response and pro-inflammatory activity were attributed to CD8+ effector T cells and nature killer cells subsets and a M1-like (high IL1B and TNF, minimal IL6) phenotypic macrophage subcluster. The colander-like lesions were dominant in the bifurcate portion, and the percentage of plasma cells was markedly increased. Immune dysregulation was induced from CD4 naïve T cells, and a downregulation of M2-like macrophage infiltration into the vascular wall. The expression of plasminogen activator, urokinase receptor, urokinase receptor (PLAUR; plasminogen activator) were observed in M2-like (high MRC1 and CD163, virtually no IL1B or TNF) macrophage in bifurcate portion. Notably, one of smooth muscle cells (SMCs) subclusters in the bifurcate portion gained more significantly myofibroblast markers than those in the main portion, and other subclusters remained the function of SMCs. CONCLUSIONS: The regions with colander-like lesions changes had more obviously T cell and macrophages driving immune-inflammatory response and SMCs differentiation, suggesting that combining therapeutic interventions after surgical removal of accessible thrombus may be beneficial. KEY POINTS: This study reveals the comprehensive cellular composition in main/lobar and bifurcate pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) specimens at the single-cell level. The bifurcate regions with colander had more obviously T cell and macrophages driving immune-inflammatory response and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) differentiation, however, the remodelling of distal or micro-vessels still remained.

The operation can remove proximal thromboembolic materials and their secondary branches. title: Incremental prognostic and risk-stratification value of ultrasound-based Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) classification for recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) is a system for stroke risk assessment. However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis. METHODS: Between January 2020 and December 2022, 231 patients with carotid plaque ipsilateral to the prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis were retrospectively screened, of whom 158 were included in the final analysis. US-based Plaque-RADS classification was assigned based on duplex US assessment of plaque features. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories and recurrent ischemic stroke. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis. The association between increasing US-based Plaque-RADS categories and the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke was assessed by trend analysis. The incremental risk-stratification value of refined high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds was quantified with net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: vs. During the 3-year follow-up period, recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 33 patients. High-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, after adjusting for smoking, homocysteine, and intraplaque neovascularization [adjusted hazard ratio: 3.56; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-11.83, P=0.038]. No statistically significant interactions were observed across the subgroups (all P for interaction >0.05). The Plaque-RADS ≥3 model demonstrated a higher AUC than the conventional US model [0.816 (95% CI: 0.731-0.901)0.810 (95% CI: 0.720-0.899)] and provided a slight net benefit across selected threshold probabilities. Additionally, the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke increased with higher Plaque-RADS categories (P for trend <0.001). Among the models using different high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds, the Plaque-RADS ≥3b model showed the best predictive performance (0.865, 95% CI: 0.799-0.930), compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model and the Plaque-RADS ≥3c model [0.824 (95% CI: 0.740-0.906)]. The Plaque-RADS ≥3b model also showed moderate improvements in NRI [0.250; (95% CI: 0.088-0.557), P=0.017] and IDI [0.090; (95% CI: 0.000-0.185), P=0.049], compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model. Bootstrap internal validation indicated limited optimism across all models. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke. The US-based Plaque-RADS may help identify plaque phenotypes associated with an increased risk of recurrent ipsilateral ischemic stroke, while refined high-risk thresholds, particularly Plaque-RADS ≥3b, may provide additional value for risk stratification.

However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.

title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution. RESULTS: XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension. CONCLUSIONS: In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients.

title: Impact of different follow-up methods on prognosis of diabetic foot patients after endovascular treatment: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus, and endovascular treatment (EVT) has become the primary revascularization strategy. However, the impact of different post-procedure follow-up methods on clinical outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the effects of seven different follow-up approaches on prognosis in DFU patients after EVT. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at three tertiary hospitals in China between June 2022 and June 2025. A total of 868 DFU patients who underwent successful EVT were enrolled and categorized into seven groups based on their primary follow-up method. The primary outcomes were 12-month wound healing rate and amputation-free survival (AFS). Secondary outcomes included major adverse limb events (MALE), reintervention rate, patient satisfaction, and glycemic control. Multivariable Cox regression and propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounders. RESULTS: Among 868 patients, the surgical hospital outpatient group demonstrated the highest 12-month wound healing rate (75.0%) and AFS rate (80.1%). The no follow-up group had the poorest outcomes (45.2% wound healing, 56.4% AFS). No follow-up was associated with significantly increased risk of MALE [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 2.15, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.62-2.85]. WeChat follow-up (aHR 1.22, 95% CI: 0.88-1.69) showed non-significant differences compared with surgical hospital outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Structured follow-up significantly improves wound healing and AFS in DFU patients after EVT. Digital health tools such as WeChat showed no statistically significant difference compared with traditional follow-up, but these observational data should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent effectiveness. The absence of follow-up is associated with substantially worse outcomes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in prospective randomized trials.

However, the impact of different post-procedure follow-up methods on clinical outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the effects of seven different follow-up approaches on prognosis in DFU patients after EVT.

title: Short-Term Outcomes of Lower-Extremity Surgical Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Among Yemeni Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen. We enrolled 39 consecutive adults with CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) who were selected for and considered fit to undergo open lower-extremity surgical revascularization between December 2022 and September 2024; follow-up was completed in December 2024. The study protocol was reviewed and approved by the Al-Thawra Hospital Ethics Committee (approval no. 33-2026), and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The study was not registered. This was an exploratory consecutive cohort; no formal sample-size calculation was performed, and no contemporaneous endovascular, nonoperative, or primary-amputation comparator group was included. Primary endpoints were graft patency and limb salvage at three months. Secondary outcomes were secondary patency, postoperative complications, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) and Vascular Quality of Life Questionnaire-6 (VascuQoL-6) scores. Paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical comparisons. RESULTS: The mean age was 60.9 years (SD 9.7), and 30 patients (76.9%) were male. Diabetes mellitus and hypertension were present in 34 (87.2%) and 30 (76.9%) patients, respectively. Nineteen patients (48.7%) had ischemic rest pain, and 20 (51.3%) had tissue loss. Great saphenous vein (GSV) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts were used in 28 (71.8%) and 11 (28.2%) patients, respectively. At three months, primary patency was 84.6% (33/39 grafts; 95% CI 70.3%-92.8%), secondary patency was 89.7% (35/39 grafts; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%), and limb salvage was 89.7% (35/39 patients; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%). Given the small cohort, the confidence intervals around these estimates were relatively wide. Among the 35 patients with limb preservation, mean ABI increased from 0.35 (SD 0.11) to 0.55 (SD 0.12; mean difference 0.21, 95% CI 0.19-0.23; p<0.001), and mean VascuQoL-6 score increased from 10.3 (SD 2.9) to 16.6 (SD 4.0; mean difference 6.3, 95% CI 5.6-7.1; p<0.001). Complications occurred in nine patients (23.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted subgroup analysis, GSV use was associated with higher primary patency than PTFE use (92.9% vs 63.6%, p=0.042). CONCLUSION: In this single-center prospective cohort, open surgical revascularization was feasible and was associated with 89.7% limb salvage and 84.6% primary patency at three months. Improvements in ABI and VascuQoL-6 were observed among patients with limb preservation. Autologous GSV use was associated with higher primary patency; this finding requires confirmation in larger, adjusted studies.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen.

title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.

title: Natural history of MRI-defined intraplaque hemorrhage-positive asymptomatic carotid stenosis in the contemporary medical era: a prospective multicenter cohort study.
abstract: The optimal management of asymptomatic carotid stenosis remains controversial despite advances in medical therapy. Although intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is an established marker of plaque vulnerability, the prospective natural history of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined IPH-positive asymptomatic carotid stenosis remains incompletely characterized. We investigated the clinical course of this population. The Stratification by Multidimensional Approach for Rational Treatment of Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis (SMART-K) study is a prospective multicenter cohort of patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis and MRI-confirmed IPH. Patients were followed for up to 36 months under medical management according to contemporary clinical practice. Baseline assessments included plaque-to-muscle (PM) ratio and soluble lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor-1 (sLOX-1). The primary endpoint was ipsilateral ischemic events, including ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and amaurosis fugax. Kaplan-Meier and exploratory Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Among 76 patients included in the final analysis, 11 (14.5%) developed primary endpoint events: ischemic stroke in 8, TIA in 2, and amaurosis fugax in 1. The 3-year cumulative incidence was 14.8%. Stenosis severity showed a trend toward association with ischemic events (hazard ratio per 10% increase, 1.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.92-2.31; P = 0.11), whereas PM ratio and sLOX-1 were not associated with events. Patients with MRI-defined IPH-positive asymptomatic carotid stenosis remained at clinically meaningful risk of ipsilateral ischemic events under contemporary clinical management. These findings provide prospective natural history data for this specifically defined population and support further evaluation of MRI-defined IPH in individualized risk-stratification strategies.

title: PERT implementation and the changing profile of patients undergoing catheter-based pulmonary embolism treatment: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Despite growing evidence supporting pulmonary embolism response teams (PERT) in high-income countries, published experience from Latin America remains scarce. We assessed the association between PERT implementation and 30-day clinical outcomes in patients with acute PE treated with catheter-based therapy (CBT) in a Latin American university hospital. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with confirmed acute PE treated with CBT between 2004 and 2025. Patients were stratified by treatment era (pre-PERT: 2004-2020; PERT: 2021-2025). The primary endpoint was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, stroke, or major bleeding (BARC grade ≥3). RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were included: 26 (49%) pre-PERT and 27 (51%) PERT era. ESC high-risk patients predominated in the pre-PERT era (17 (65%) vs 6 (22%); p = 0.002), while intermediate-high risk predominated in the PERT era (9 (35%) vs 21 (78%); p = 0.002). Dedicated thrombectomy devices were used universally in the PERT era (14 (54%) vs 27 (100%); p < 0.001). MACE occurred in 10 (38%) vs 4 (15%) patients (p = 0.06). In a subanalysis restricted to intermediate-high risk patients, 30-day mortality was 0/21 (0%) in the PERT era versus 3/9 (33%) in the pre-PERT era (p = 0.021). CONCLUSIONS: In one of the few Latin American reports on PERT-guided CBT, implementation was associated with a shift toward intermediate-high risk patients, greater use of mechanical thrombectomy, and lower thrombolytic exposure, without an increase in major bleeding. Among intermediate-high risk patients, 30-day mortality was significantly lower in the PERT era, supporting the safety and potential benefit of structured multidisciplinary PE management in resource-limited settings.

We assessed the association between PERT implementation and 30-day clinical outcomes in patients with acute PE treated with catheter-based therapy (CBT) in a Latin American university hospital. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with confirmed acute PE treated with CBT between 2004 and 2025.

title: Association between age and in-hospital mortality and arch repair strategy in acute type A aortic dissection: a dose-response analysis of a retrospective cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced age is a recognized risk factor in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but its dose-response relationship with in-hospital mortality and the optimal extent of arch repair in elderly patients remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. The association between age (as a continuous variable) and in-hospital mortality was assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis. In a subgroup of elderly patients (≥60 years, n=115), perioperative outcomes between no/partial arch replacement and total arch replacement were compared after 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. RESULTS: vs. Among 1,042 included patients, overall in-hospital mortality was 3.7% (39/1,042), and median age was 51 (interquartile range, 40-59) years. Age was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.04 per year, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.07, P=0.01), and RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear association without evidence of a threshold effect (P overall =0.02; P for non-linearity =0.31). In the elderly subgroup (n=244), 115 patients met imaging eligibility criteria for PSM, yielding 30 matched pairs. In this small matched cohort, total arch replacement was associated with longer cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, with no statistically significant differences in mortality (6.7%3.3%) or major complications. CONCLUSIONS: Age shows a continuous linear association with in-hospital mortality after ATAAD repair, without evidence of a threshold effect. In elderly patients, total arch replacement and limited arch repair showed no statistically significant differences in early outcomes in this small matched cohort, suggesting that operative strategy should be individualized based on anatomical and physiological risk rather than age alone-a finding that warrants validation in larger studies.

This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024.

title: Real-world outcomes of endoanchors in the prevention and treatment of proximal endograft failure in a multicenter registry.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the outcomes of the Heli-FX EndoAnchor system (ESAR) in the prevention and treatment of proximal endograft failure after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective data analysis from a multicenter registry of patients treated by ESAR (2017-2025). In the prevention group (PG), endoanchors were used to prevent proximal endograft failure during primary EVAR. In the treatment group (TG), endoanchors were used to treat a type IA endoleak and/or migration after a previous EVAR. End points were technical success, procedural success, and freedom from proximal endograft failure (new-onset type IA endoleak, related reintervention, endograft migration). RESULTS: There were 325 patients, 234 (72%) in the PG and 91 (28%) in the TG. Technical success was 100% in the PG and 97% in TG (P = .043), with a procedural success of 100% vs 88% (P < .001). After 5 years of follow-up (median, 42 months), freedom from proximal endograft failure was 90.2% [95% confidence interval (CI), 85-95] in the PG and 74.9% (95% CI, 64-87) in the TG (P = .001). Neck length <7 mm [hazard ratio (HR), 2.11; 95% CI, 1.18-4.56; P < .001] and use of endoanchors as a treatment (HR, 3.48; 95% CI, 1.61-7.51; P < .001) had a higher risk of proximal endograft failure. In the TG, the use of endoanchors alone (without a proximal aortic extension; HR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.19-8.65; P < .001) and the persistence of a type IA endoleak at the completion angiography (HR, 15.9; 95% CI, 10.5-23.0; P < .001) were associated with a higher risk of proximal failure. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, ESAR was used as an adjunct during primary EVAR in patients with a hostile proximal neck and as a salvage treatment of proximal endograft failure after a previous EVAR, with favorable success rates in both settings. In the preventive setting, outcomes were less favorable when the anatomical proximal neck length was <7 mm. In the treatment of type IA endoleak, favorable results were obtained in up to 80% of cases, with a higher success rate when endoanchors were combined with a proximal aortic extension, and the persistence of a type IA endoleak on the completion angiogram was a negative prognostic factor. Future comparative studies are necessary to better clarify the clinical efficacy of ESAR in a prevention and treatment setting.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the outcomes of the Heli-FX EndoAnchor system (ESAR) in the prevention and treatment of proximal endograft failure after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective data analysis from a multicenter registry of patients treated by ESAR (2017-2025). In the prevention group (PG), endoanchors were used to prevent proximal endograft failure during primary EVAR.

title: One-year outcomes of percutaneous deep vein arterialization in the Dutch LimFlow registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous deep vein arterialization (pDVA) offers a potential endovascular alternative for reducing the risk of major amputation in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) who have no standard revascularization options "no-option" CLTI (NO-CLTI). METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included limb salvage, overall survival, patency, pain scores, wound healing, transcutaneous oxygen pressure, and quality of life (QoL). RESULTS: A total of 26 limbs of 23 patients with NO-CLTI (median age, 67.0 (52.0-72.0) years; 20 men) were included, all classified as Rutherford category 5 and 17/22 (77.3%) as Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection stage 4. Thirteen (56.5%) patients suffered from diabetes mellitus and five (21.7%) from renal insufficiency. Technical success was 100%. Amputation-free survival was 69.2%, limb salvage 80.8%, and overall survival 88.5% at 12 months. Primary patency, primary-assisted patency, and secondary patency rates at 12 months were 6.6%, 27.3%, and 35.7%, respectively. Reinterventions were performed to maintain patency in 85% of the limbs and 58% for maturation of the pDVA. Median time to wound healing was 6.9 months, with 73.4% healed at 12 months. Pain scores decreased significantly (P <.001) in 12 months. QoL improved from a mean of 37% to 68% on the VascuQoL-25, though these analyses were based on limited available data. CONCLUSIONS: pDVA in patients with NO-CLTI is safe and effective at 12 months, preventing major amputation and mortality in the majority of patients. QoL also appeared to improve following pDVA. These observations warrant confirmation in larger studies. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study strengthens existing evidence on the effectivity and safety of percutaneous deep vein arterialization using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical) in patients with "no-option" chronic limb-threatening ischemia. Our data demonstrated a 100% technical success rate and comparable amputation-free survival and limb salvage to other percutaneous deep vein arterialization studies. Notably, this prospective and well-phenotyped cohort uniquely incorporated patient-reported outcome measures, showing improvements in pain, transcutaneous oxygen pressure and quality of life.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months.

title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Identifies Central Role for Inflammatory Pathways.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Epigenetic mechanisms underlying susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) remain poorly understood. Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways. METHODS: We first conducted an epigenome-wide association study of incident AAA (1324 cases and 42 065 noncases), performed stratified analyses by population group and smoking status, and conducted Mendelian randomization to facilitate causal inference of the CpG-AAA association. Chromatin state, island context, and transcription factor binding were implicated through functional annotation of identified CpGs. To identify genes impacted by change in methylation state, we aligned associations with transcriptional data obtained in blood, aorta, and liver. We performed expression quantitative trait methylation to capture CpG-gene-expression links across the genome. Network Mendelian randomization was used to test cardiometabolic and inflammatory mediation. Finally, we developed a methylation risk score for AAA using penalized regression and evaluated its performance against a clinical model in the Million Veteran Program and 2 external studies. RESULTS: AGER, C2 DDR1 LDLR TRIB1 Epigenome-wide association study identified 1253 CpGs associated with incident AAA, and Mendelian randomization supported a putative causal role for 143 of these associations. Functional annotation pointed to predominantly distal, enhancer-centered regulation and enrichment of inflammatory transcription factor programs (eg, activator protein-1 and nuclear factor κB). This distal architecture was consistent with expression quantitative trait methylation results, which showed a larger number of trans associations. Among 143 CpGs associated with AAA in Mendelian randomization analyses, we identified 213 CpG-gene expression pairs with strong colocalization support, including, and. Multi-trait colocalization further prioritized 8 CpG-gene expression-AAA links with evidence of a shared genetic signal. Network Mendelian randomization identified 135 putative mediation pathways linking CpGs to AAA, including 58 via cardiometabolic traits and 77 via inflammation-related traits. Blood lipid traits mediated >40% of the associations between AAA risk and CpGs near(cg19305903) and(cg14128479). Among inflammation-related mediators, circulating DAG1, NEXN, MMP9, IL1RN, and MMP13 were prioritized as potential intermediates. Additionally, a CpG selection process was used to develop a methylation risk score for AAA, which strongly associated with disease in both the discovery cohort and 2 external validation cohorts, even after adjustment for a full suite of clinical covariates. CONCLUSIONS: This study identified putative causal DNA methylation markers for AAA, and multi-omics analyses implicate activator protein-1-linked inflammatory transcriptional programs, blood lipids, and multiple inflammation-related proteins as key pathways underlying methylation-associated AAA risk.

title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database. METHODS: Patients who underwent AD surgery were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (MIMIC-IV; development cohort) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external evaluation cohort). The primary outcome was postoperative GIB within 30 days, defined using a composite database-derived algorithm requiring either (I) a hemoglobin (Hb) decrease of ≥2 g/dL accompanied by at least one supporting indicator, including a transfusion record, hemostatic medication use, or endoscopic examination; or (II) the combination of a transfusion record and a GIB diagnosis. An isolated Hb decrease or transfusion record was not sufficient for outcome classification. Routinely available demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and disease-severity variables were extracted. Records with missing values in variables required for the final analysis were excluded before model development. Multivariable logistic regression served as the baseline model, with XGB and random forest employed as comparator models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 935 patients (GIB incidence, 10.7%), whereas the eICU-CRD validation cohort comprised 542 patients (GIB incidence, 12.7%). In the development cohort, the AUCs were 0.887 for logistic regression, 0.962 for XGB, and 0.853 for random forest. In the eICU-CRD cohort, XGB yielded an AUC point estimate of 0.873. CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective two-database analysis developed prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery. The models showed discrimination in the analyzed data; however, prospective validation using predictors measured within prespecified pre-event windows is required before clinical implementation.

title: Post-operative multi-organ dysfunction following heart transplantation and left ventricular assist device implantation: phenotypes, trajectories, and prognostic implications-a retrospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multi-organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is a leading cause of mortality after heart transplantation (HTx) and left ventricular assist device (LVAD), yet its phenotypic heterogeneity remains poorly characterised. This study intends to identify and clinically validate distinct multi-organ dysfunction phenotypes following HTx and LVAD implantation, and to analyse their early prognosis using longitudinal biomarker trajectories and independent clinical adjudication. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 68 consecutive adult patients who underwent HTx or LVAD implantation in the Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery Department of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, between January 2020 and June 2025. The Institutional Review Board of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology approved this with a waiver of informed consent. We collected demographic, preoperative, and operative data from medical records. Postoperative MODS was defined by Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) criteria as dysfunction with ≥2 organ systems. Patients were followed up for inpatient, 1-, and 2-year mortality. RESULTS: vs. vs. vs. vs. vs. vs. MODS occurred in 48 of 68 patients (70.6%). It was more frequent after HTx than LVAD (77.6%52.6%, P=0.08). The most common organ dysfunctions were cardiovascular (70.6%), hepatic (60.3%), and respiratory (50.0%). Patients with MODS had significantly longer cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) duration than those without MODS (183.11±57.42138.28±29.83 min; P=0.003) and higher rates of respiratory (68.8%5.0%; P<0.001), cardiovascular (83.3%40.0%; P=0.001), and renal dysfunction (50.0%5.0%; P=0.001). After adjustment, MODS was independently associated with 2-year mortality [hazard ratio (HR) =5.47, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-27.9; P=0.04]. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified 2 MODS phenotypes: a high-severity/multi-system phenotype with high probabilities of renal (100%), hepatic (78%), and respiratory (72%) dysfunction, and a lower-severity/selective phenotype. The high-severity phenotype had significantly worse 2-year survival than the lower-severity phenotype (44.8%74.4%; log-rank P=0.005). CONCLUSIONS: With regard to post-cardiac surgery MODS, we report a novel trajectory-based approach that holds promise for improving early risk stratification and guiding targeted management by distinguishing high-severity multisystem from low-severity selective trajectories following HTx and LVAD implantation.

title: The gut microbiome and vascular disease - A systematic review of mechanistic insights and implications for vascular surgery.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Observational studies repeatedly linked gut microbial features and metabolites to vascular disease, but it is unclear which associations are reproducible, which remain significant after confounder adjustment, and how they relate to experimental evidence. This review aims to determine which taxa and metabolites are consistently associated across independent human studies; whether the population, phenotype, method, and sample type explain divergent findings; and where the human data converge with, diverge from, or remain untested with the animal and interventional literature. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched for human studies of the gut microbiome composition or gut-derived metabolites reporting atherosclerotic, aneurysmal, peripheral arterial, calcific, or arterial stiffness outcomes from database inception to December 31, 2025. Study screening and duplicate article extraction were conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. The study design was classified explicitly, the covariates in each primary analysis were extracted, and the risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. The findings were then compared with the animal and human interventional literature identified through targeted searching. RESULTS: Roseburia intestinalis All the 29 included reports were observational (19 cross-sectional, 3 case-control, and 7 cohort) studies, and none was interventional. The reproducible findings were the enrichment of Proteobacteria-affiliated genera (5 reports) and of oral-origin organisms (3 reports), and the depletion of butyrate producers in carotid disease. The carnitine pathway intermediates gamma-butyrobetaine and trimethyllysine were independently associated with cardiovascular death and major adverse limb events (hazard ratio, 1.93; 95% confidence interval, 1.35-2.76) in two independent cohorts. Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) was outcome-specific; TMAO levels were associated with 5-year mortality in peripheral arterial disease (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.06; 95% confidence interval, 1.36-3.11) and with ankle-brachial-index-defined disease in diabetes (odds ratio, 1.051), but TMAO levels were lower in large-artery stroke than in controls and were unrelated to carotid or limb outcomes once renal function was modelled. In addition, 16 of 29 reports fitted a multivariable model, and only three included renal function; the compositional findings were almost exclusively unadjusted. The risk of bias was good in 11 reports, moderate in 16, and low in 2. Animal models causally implicate TMAO in atherogenesis and aneurysm formation and show butyrate andto be protective, but the results of germ-free experiments and the only human fecal transplantation trial are discordant. CONCLUSIONS: A small number of gut microbial signals are reproducible, but most have not been adjusted for potential confounders, particularly renal function, which may partly explain the observed associations. The carnitine pathway metabolites with the strongest prognostic signal in surgical populations have never been tested in an animal vascular model. Microbiome profiling has no current role in vascular surgical practice.
